summary.one_liner: Qwen3-VL is Alibaba Qwen's open vision-language model family (Dense and MoE, Instruct and Thinking editions) for image, video, OCR, GUI-agent and grounding tasks.
summary.what_it_does: The README introduces Qwen3-VL as a multimodal model family available in Dense and MoE architectures, with Instruct and reasoning-enhanced Thinking variants, and lists model sizes from 2B to 235B-A22B. It describes capabilities including operating PC and mobile GUIs, generating Draw.io/HTML/CSS/JS from images or videos, 2D and 3D grounding, a native 256K context (expandable to 1M), video understanding with timestamps, and OCR across 32 languages. Quickstart code shows loading the model with Hugging Face Transformers for single-image, multi-image, video and batch inference, plus controls for pixel and frame budgets via the processor and the qwen-vl-utils package. Deployment sections cover vLLM and SGLang servers, offline inference, a Gradio-style web UI, and a Docker image. The README also covers YaRN configuration for long contexts and a hosted API option through DashScope.
use_cases: describe or caption images and videos
read text and extract information from documents
automate PC or mobile GUI tasks with a visual agent
generate HTML or code from screenshots or mockups
locate objects with 2D or 3D bounding boxes
serve a multimodal model with vLLM or SGLang
notable: Dense and MoE model sizes with Instruct and Thinking editions, including FP8 checkpoints
Native 256K context extendable to 1M tokens via YaRN configuration
Interleaved-MRoPE, DeepStack and text-timestamp alignment architecture updates
Fine-grained visual token budget control for images and videos, plus fps or frame sampling for video
Ready-made Docker image and web demo for local use
caveats: The largest models (e.g. 235B-A22B) require multi-GPU setups such as 8x H100/H200 in the README's serving examples
Several cookbooks are listed as being prepared and have no content yet
Video decoding depends on optional backends; the README notes decord has known hangs and is no longer maintained, and torchcodec needs FFmpeg
